recommendation: Keep the existing audit commit as-is and do not publish a duplicate. Future jurisdiction-specific tax-type breakdowns should be handled by profiles/extensions or a new tracker rather than changing the base resources under FHIR-29689.
issue_request: FHIR-29689 was a Published/Persuasive Financial Management R5 change request asking to add tax support at Claim item/detail/subDetail, ClaimResponse addItem/detail/subDetail, and ExplanationOfBenefit item/detail/subDetail plus addItem/detail/subDetail. The approved resolution selected a single `.tax 0..1 Money` element for the affected structures, left tax breakdowns to extensions, and said jurisdictional implementation guides/profiles should handle jurisdiction-specific tax treatment.
initial_application: No current repository commit message explicitly names FHIR-29689. Git history shows commit 75e9d09e288b16ae6531e19fbaffff9380ebf942 added the tax elements and shared financial-module tax guidance to the Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit sources.
additional_context: FHIR-30926 is a tightly related later Published/Persuasive with Modification issue; its final comment says it has the same resolution as FHIR-29689 and it is already represented on the combined branch by commit 12fe8673ecdf1d632af12885611c1ac5084a42fc. The active build configuration includes Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit.
reconciliation: No new source change or commit was published because the combined branch already contains `Issue-Reconcile-Key: FHIR-29689` in commit e293af64011f5815598b8f047ec5917133e6b5c9. Current authoritative StructureDefinition source contains the requested `.tax 0..1 Money` elements in all approved Claim-family line/addItem structures.
